App Hosting deploy provisions the default compute service account on
every
run, creating it and granting it IAM roles. The catch blocks only
ignored 409
(create) and 400 (roles), so a least-privilege deploy identity that
lacks
iam.serviceAccounts.create or resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy got
a 403
that was rethrown, hard-failing the deploy even when the service account
already existed and worked.
Treat 403 in both catch blocks as a warning-and-continue so deploys from
restricted identities are no longer blocked.

1.16.0 (August 26, 2026)

NEW FEATURES:

  • Terraform now stores planned private data for providers, allowing provider-specific state to be preserved across plan and apply. (#37986)

  • terraform_data: The new store block can hold ephemeral and sensitive values across plan and apply. (#38298)

  • Providers can now use nested blocks as computed values (#38305)

  • import: import blocks inside modules are now supported. (#38352)

  • Terraform is now available as a pre-built binary for Linux s390x (zLinux). (#38384)

  • Resource action triggers can now use on_failure modes of halt, taint, or continue. (#38722)

ENHANCEMENTS:

  • state show: The state show command can now produce machine-readable output when supplied with the -json flag (#23940)

  • workspace: The workspace list command can now produce machine-readable output when supplied with the -json flag (#38397)

  • test: Terraform now reports which resources were left behind when skip_cleanup is set. (#38449)

  • stacks: Action configurations now have access to a caller symbol containing the object value of the calling resource. (#38668)

  • Actions can now use before_destroy and after_destroy events. (#38668)

  • cloud: Terraform now displays a summary of policy evaluation outcomes for plan and apply runs against HCP Terraform. (#38715)

  • policy: Terraform now resolves policy plugin credentials from the configured cloud or remote backend during init, plan, and apply, rather than requiring the plugin to read credentials itself. (#38716)

  • graph: The terraform graph command can now output graphs in Mermaid format using the -format=mermaid flag. (#38719)

  • Child module outputs with unreferenced deprecated nested attributes no longer return deprecation warnings. (#38778)

  • Resource lifecycle blocks now support destroy = false to prevent a resource from being destroyed. (#38784)

  • The contains() function can now test for null values. (#38792)

  • console: The terraform console command now accepts an optional -scope= flag, which can be used to evaluate expressions within the scope of a module or a specific module instance. (#31861)

  • -invoke can now be combined with -target to specify the calling resource instance when multiple resources trigger the same action. (#38845)

  • The terraform stacks command now automatically infers the target hostname from the local credentials file (credentials.tfrc.json) when neither TF_STACKS_HOSTNAME nor TF_CLOUD_HOSTNAME is set (#38896)

BUG FIXES:

  • import blocks now correctly respect provider local names. (#38338)

  • terraform apply no longer panics when the plan contains a no-op change for a deposed resource that has lifecycle.precondition or lifecycle.postcondition blocks. (#38586)

  • workspace: Terraform now raises an error if an invalid workspace name becomes selected due to out-of-band changes. (#38594)

  • test: Terraform now raises a warning when a file referenced via the -filter flag does not exist. (#38603)

  • init: Terraform no longer removes locks from the dependency lock file for providers configured as dev_override. (#38634)

  • init: Terraform now warns when unmanaged providers are in use and may impact provider installation. (#38656)

  • Actions are now invoked with respect to all resource dependencies. (#38668)

  • Terraform now returns the correct error when an import target exists in state but has no corresponding configuration. (#38782)

  • The merge() function no longer panics when passed null objects. (#38792)

  • Allow underscores in provider source address namespaces, so private registry provider addresses are no longer rejected as invalid (#38894)

  • test: Optional ephemeral values do not have to be set at plan time (#38974)

NOTES:

  • init: Errors due to incompatible -upgrade and -lockfile=readonly flags are now raised earlier in the init process. (#38561)

UPGRADE NOTES:

  • bastion_host_key is now correctly applied by provisioners. Review your provisioner configurations to verify the configured key is correct before upgrading. (#38318)

fix: report query policy unknown and N/A statuses

Permit n/a as an intentional fifth JSON status value for overall_result
and per-identity result fields. The producer emits "n/a" when no policies
matched a resource (pass result with empty policies array); the parser must
accept it in both positions.

Add queryPolicyResultNA to validQueryPolicyResult so ParsePolicyQuerySummary
no longer rejects n/a wire records, and add an N/A branch to toPolicyResultLabel
so n/a summaries render as "N/A" in human output rather than "Unknown".

Validation rules:
- n/a is valid in overall_result and per-identity result fields.
- An n/a identity row must carry an empty policies array; non-empty is malformed.
- n/a is not valid as a per-policy result.
- Legacy pass-with-empty-policies rows continue to be accepted.

Also include supporting changes from the original commit:
- Report unavailable configuration and incomplete callback relationships as
  Unknown by mapping policy.UnknownResult explicitly in
  queryPolicyResultFromEvaluation.
- Route unconsumed diagnostics back to the caller via AddResult's second
  return value to avoid silently dropping unmatched error diagnostics.
- Key PolicyMetadata by (address, policy-set-name, source-path) instead of
  address alone so same-address policies from distinct sets are stored and
  sorted independently.
- Preserve associated diagnostics per policy identity, target metadata,
  source ranges, and race-free concurrent rendering.

Add focused unit, integration, serialization, command, and race coverage:
- Parser: accept n/a overall, n/a identity row with empty policies, mixed n/a
  and pass; reject n/a identity row with non-empty policies, per-policy n/a.
- Producer round-trip: all-n/a and mixed n/a/pass summaries survive
  serialisation and re-parsing through ParsePolicyQuerySummary.
- Human renderer: all-n/a header shows N/A (not Unknown); mixed n/a and pass
  shows N/A per row; "Unknown" does not appear when all rows are n/a.
- Cloud log renderer: all-n/a and mixed-n/a fixture records render correctly.
- Callback semantics, error metadata, status precedence, exact hook emission,
  stable JSON arrays, and queries without policy arguments.

新增 API 输出格式与查询

API 调用新增统一的响应格式化和查询能力：

  • --output：支持 json（默认）、table、table-num、text、yaml 和 off。
  • --query：使用 JMESPath 在格式化前筛选或投影完整响应，路径通常从 Result.* 开始。
  • 查询和输出过程保留精确数字，避免大整数和高精度小数丢失。
  • 表格与文本输出保留 ResponseMetadata，并按查询字段顺序展示；文本使用完整字段路径，YAML 对对象键稳定排序。

示例：

ve ecs DescribeInstances \
  --query "Result.Instances" \
  --output table

Skills 安装流程优化

  • @volcengine/skills-setup 会根据已有 ve 版本选择安装路径：ve >= 1.1.3 使用 ve skills update，旧版本自动使用兼容安装流程。
  • 新增 --update，可将 ve 和 arkcli 强制升级到 @latest。
  • 首次安装 ve 时不再重复执行 Skill 安装。
  • 新增通用 Agent 调用方识别，支持通过 AGENT / IS_AGENT 标识调用来源。

稳定性修复

  • 无效或不完整的 --query 表达式现在返回明确错误，不再触发 panic。
  • 修复表格、文本、YAML 输出中的字段遗漏、顺序不稳定和数值精度问题。
  • 修复 Go 1.17 下输出模块的编译兼容性。

升级

ve upgrade --version 1.1.4

或通过 npm：

npm install -g @volcengine/cli@1.1.4

完整变更：v1.1.3...v1.1.4

新增 Skill 管理

新增火山引擎 Agent Skill 的安装、更新和卸载能力：

ve skills install
ve skills update
ve skills uninstall
  • install：安装尚未安装的核心 Skill。
  • update：更新到最新版本，并补充缺失的核心 Skill。
  • uninstall：卸载由 ve 管理的 Skill，同时保护存在本地修改的内容。

核心 Skill 默认安装到：

  • ~/.agents/skills
  • ~/.claude/skills

检测到 OpenClaw、Hermes Agent 或 Trae 时，也会安装到对应的 Skill 目录。Codex、Cursor 和 OpenCode 可直接读取 ~/.agents/skills。

npm 安装集成

  • 通过 npm 安装或升级 @volcengine/cli 时，自动安装或更新核心 Skill。
  • 可设置以下环境变量跳过自动安装：
VOLCENGINE_CLI_SKIP_SKILLS=1
  • 自动安装失败后，可运行 ve skills update 重试。

功能更新

CLI 自升级

  • 新增 ve upgrade，支持升级到最新版本或指定版本。
  • 自动识别 standalone、npm 和 Homebrew 安装来源，并采用对应的升级方式。
  • standalone 升级支持 SHA256 校验、原子替换和失败回滚。
  • 新增后台版本检查及每日一次的升级提醒，可通过 VOLCENGINE_CLI_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=1 关闭。

泛化 OpenAPI 调用

  • 新增 --force，支持调用本地元数据尚未收录的 Service 或 Action。

  • 新增 --version 和 --method，可指定 OpenAPI 版本及 HTTP 方法。

  • 未收录的 Service 可配合固定 Endpoint 调用：

    ve newservice DescribeNewResource \
  --version 2024-01-01 \
  --endpoint open.volcengineapi.com \
  --SomeParam value \
  --force

请求参数能力

  • CLI 系统参数统一使用双横线形式，并放在 Action 之后，例如 --profile、--region、--endpoint 和 --lang。
  • 新增可重复使用的 --header Name=Value，支持自定义 HTTP 请求头。
  • 新增 --body，支持直接传递 JSON 请求体。
  • 加强 JSON Body、Content-Type、参数冲突及未知参数的校验和处理。

帮助信息

  • Action 的默认帮助改为简洁模式，展示参数名称、类型及是否必填。
  • 新增 --detail，用于查看完整参数描述和示例。
  • 内置更丰富的 OpenAPI 参数说明，并改进中英文帮助信息。

稳定性改进

  • 修复自升级过程中的并发、版本回退、下载源切换及 Windows 文件替换问题。
  • 修复系统参数与 API 同名参数的解析冲突。

A nested text label carried the record number as soon as a list held more
than one element, so `$1 == "RESULT.INSTANCELIST.TAGS"` matched a
one-record response and then silently matched nothing once a second record
came back. Labels are now the field path alone, and a record's nested lines
are attributed by following that record's own row, as the AWS CLI text
formatter does. Only `table` still numbers its sections: it prints every
record before any nested section and has no adjacent row to rely on.

A shared column that was a scalar on one record and structured on another
reported None, which is how a row reports a field that is absent or null,
while `table` showed the real value in the same cell. It now renders the
value inline, or points at the flattened lines below when those lines
actually exist.

text and table emitted one write syscall per rendered line at an unbuffered
stdout; a 20k-record response cost 60k syscalls. Output is now batched
behind a writer that keeps the Unwrap chain intact, so terminal-width
fitting still finds the underlying file.

The --query column-order hint no longer follows the renderer below the
level the multiselect hash projected, matching what buildSections already
did for table sections.

description:
Enable LTO for linux release and glibc CLI builds in CI (#25126)

## Changes

- Enable thin [LTO](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ThinLTO.html) for
(alpha) releases and glibc CLI builds in CI. Omit LTO for PRs (too
slow).
- Increase parallel linker jobs for GCC/Clang to 8.
- Fix release CLI link error (missing symbols).

Issue: https://github.com/duckdblabs/duckdb-internal/issues/4354.

### Job structure

```
prepare
├── linux-release (glibc matrix)
│   ├── linux-release-tests
│   ├── linux-configs
│   ├── regression (PR only)
│   └── staged-extension-install
├── linux-release-musl (musl matrix)
└── other platform/test jobs
```

### LTO and cache warmup

We want to adopt LTO for (alpha) release builds, but LTO increases the
build time by 2-3x, so we keep a non-LTO build for PR CI runs.

The second problem is that LTO cache entries cannot be used for non-LTO
builds. So, it is important to create a non-LTO build since the workflow
`Main.yml` populates the ccache entries of all future PR CI runs.

For an (alpha) release, we create an optimized (LTO) and compatibility
(non-LTO) build in `linux-release`:
- The optimized build uses link-time optimization. LTO has a very low
cache hit rate, so ccache is disabled.
- The compatibility build is used to warm up the caches used by the next
CI runs.

### Static/shared library file

The static `libduckdb.a` file always come from the non-LTO builds,
preserving compatibility with GCC, Clang without LTO, and differing
downstream build flags.

Shared-library and CLI release artifacts come from the canonical build
(with LTO for releases).

Since we use Clang 20+, we want to verify that:
- Compatibility static libraries work from a GCC C client.
- Canonical shared libraries work from a GCC C client.

So we check we never ship broken shared or static libraries in an
(alpha) release.

## Results

Recently, we changed toolchains and compiler flags:
- [enabled](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/24391) modern CPU
instructions (`-march=x86-v64-v3`) for the CLI.
- [switched](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/25053/) from GCC 14
to Clang 20+ for most CI jobs.

This PR enables LTO on top of the Clang changes, so we want to compare:
1. old: GCC-14, no `-march`,
2. current: Clang 20+ with `-march=x86-v64-v3`,
3. new: Clang 20+ with LTO and `-march=x86-v64-v3`.

Important: the **measurements include changes in the last three weeks
from other contributors**, so it's not "only" toolchain and/or compiler
flag changes.

### Extension (uncompressed) binary size

Extension | GCC-14, no `-march` | Clang 20+, `-march=v3` | Clang 20+,
LTO, `-march=v3`
-- | -- | -- | --
autocomplete | 13.5 MiB | 48.6 MiB (+260.8%) | 13.6 MiB (+1.0%)
core_functions | 32.2 MiB | 60.0 MiB (+86.3%) | 35.9 MiB (+11.5%)
fts | 14.6 MiB | 50.2 MiB (+243.6%) | 10.2 MiB (-30.2%)
httpfs | 23.9 MiB | 57.9 MiB (+142.5%) | 23.4 MiB (-2.0%)
icu | 23.8 MiB | 50.2 MiB (+111.1%) | 15.1 MiB (-36.5%)
inet | 13.7 MiB | 49.1 MiB (+257.9%) | 8.9 MiB (-35.1%)
json | 40.9 MiB | 49.5 MiB (+21.0%) | 41.9 MiB (+2.4%)
parquet | 21.2 MiB | 52.0 MiB (+145.1%) | 22.5 MiB (+6.0%)
tpcds | 25.6 MiB | 50.9 MiB (+98.5%) | 27.0 MiB (+5.3%)
tpch | 24.4 MiB | 49.6 MiB (+103.1%) | 25.7 MiB (+5.2%)

### Benchmark runtime (geomean)

| Benchmark | GCC 13 | GCC 14, march=v3 | Clang 20+, march=v3 | Clang
20+, march=v3, LTO |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AoC24 | 160 ms | 162 ms (+1.4%) | 150 ms (-6.5%) | 136 ms (-14.7%) |
| CSV | 295 ms | 276 ms (-6.4%) | 265 ms (-10.1%) | 270 ms (-8.5%) |
| H2OAI | 414 ms | 380 ms (-8.1%) | 348 ms (-15.9%) | 322 ms (-22.2%) |
| IMDB | 131 ms | 97 ms (-25.8%) | 121 ms (-7.6%) | 115 ms (-12.5%) |
| Ingestion Perf | 852 ms | 786 ms (-7.7%) | 791 ms (-7.1%) | 733 ms
(-13.9%) |
| Micro | 248 ms | 259 ms (+4.4%) | 238 ms (-3.9%) | 215 ms (-13.3%) |
| RealNest | 131 ms | 139 ms (+5.9%) | 109 ms (-16.9%) | 73 ms (-44.0%)
|

(-18.2%) |
| TPCDS SF10 | n/a¹ | 83 ms | 75 ms (-9.4%) | 56 ms (-32.1%) |
| TPCH SF10 | 114 ms | 135 ms (+18.2%) | 116 ms (+1.7%) | 90 ms (-21.0%)
|

¹ The GCC 13 run ran TPCDS at SF3, while the GCC 14, Clang, and Clang
LTO runs used SF10



I've created duckdblabs/duckdb-internal/issues/10585 to analyse
the regressions

Geomean GCC -> Clang regressions:
| Benchmark | GCC 13 | GCC 14, march=v3 | Clang 20+, march=v3 | Clang
20+, march=v3, LTO |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| IMDB | 131 ms | **97 ms (-25.8%)** | **121 ms (-7.6%)** | 115 ms
(-12.5%) |

CPU baseline v3 regressions:

| Benchmark | GCC 13 | GCC 14, march=v3 | Clang 20+, march=v3 | Clang
20+, march=v3, LTO |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AoC24 | 160 ms | 162 ms (+1.4%) | 150 ms (-6.5%) | 136 ms (-14.7%) |
| Micro | 248 ms | **259 ms (+4.4%)** | 238 ms (-3.9%) | 215 ms (-13.3%)
|
| RealNest | 131 ms | **139 ms (+5.9%)** | 109 ms (-16.9%) | 73 ms
(-44.0%) |
| TPCH SF10 | 114 ms | **135 ms (+18.2%)** | 116 ms (+1.7%) | 90 ms
(-21.0%) |
| TPCH-PARQUET SF1 | 46 ms | **50 ms (+8.5%)** | 50 ms (+8.8%) | 38 ms
(-16.2%) |




Using an unweighted arithmetic mean across the 10 benchmarks with a
common GCC 13 baseline:

| Configuration | Average improvement vs. GCC 13 |
|---|---:|
| GCC 14, march=v3 | 2.2% faster |
| Clang 20+, march=v3 | 6.9% faster |
| Clang 20+, march=v3, LTO | 18.5% faster |

TPCDS is excluded because its GCC 13 run used SF3. Including TPCDS
relative to its GCC 14 SF10 baseline changes the Clang averages to 7.1%
and 19.7%, respectively.

## Future work

In the future, we can:
- enable LTO for other platforms (macOS, Windows, Musl-based).
- add more advanced optimizations like
[PGO](https://llvm.org/docs/HowToBuildWithPGO.html),
[AutoFDO](https://github.com/google/autofdo),
[Bolt](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/bolt/docs/OptimizingClang.md),
and/or [Propeller](https://github.com/google/llvm-propeller) to the
"optimized" build.

description:
feat(ci): release shared-OpenSSL packages for ppc64le and s390x MONGOSH-1681 (#2826)

PR #2779 added the ppc64le/s390x shared-OpenSSL build variants by editing
.evergreen.yml directly. That file is generated by
`npm run update-evergreen-config` from .evergreen/evergreen.yml.in and the
generators in .evergreen/build-variants/, so the next automated regeneration
on main reverted all of it. It also only made the binaries compile; nothing
packaged, signed or published them, because that side is driven by
config/release-package-matrix.js.

This redoes the change at the source level:

- compile-build-variants.js: openssl11/openssl3 compile variants for
  linux-ppc64le (rhel8-power-small) and linux-s390x (rhel7-zseries-large),
  mirroring the existing x64/arm64 entries.
- e2e-tests-build-variants.js: matching e2e variants on rhel9-power-small and
  rhel9-zseries-small.
- release-package-matrix.js: tgz + rpm entries for the four new
  executableOsIds, which is what generates the package_artifact_*,
  sign_artifact_*, verify_artifact_* and barque publishing tasks. Reuses the
  existing ppc64le/s390x descriptions and serverLikeTargetLists, and the same
  packageType spelling as x64/arm64 so the download centre groups them
  correctly.
- evergreen.yml.in: attach the generated pkg_test_rpmextract_* smoke tests to
  the existing ppc64le/s390x smoke-test variants. OpenSSL 1.1 packages are
  tested on RHEL 8 and OpenSSL 3 on RHEL 9, matching the OpenSSL each release
  actually ships; RHEL 7 s390x keeps only the static build. Without this the
  tasks are generated but attached to no variant, so they never run.
- Regenerated .evergreen.yml (44 new tasks, no existing task removed).

ALL_PACKAGE_VARIANTS grows from 26 to 34, so the two hardcoded counts in the
build package tests are updated; the build-variant assertion is broadened to
loop over the OpenSSL tags instead of only the untagged names.

The compile-artifact.sh and signable-compiler.ts fixes from #2779 are in
source files and survived, so they are not repeated here.

runner just stays `running` through the whole build and bitballoon can't
distinguish "the agent is thinking" from "the agent is done, the preview
is building". The fix is to link at deploy *creation* instead, which
means the runner ids have to reach the `createSiteDeploy` request.

create-deploy body. One-field passthrough; no change to the deploy flow.

- **`src/utils/deploy/deploy-source.ts`** (new) —
`getDeploySourceFields()` returns `deploy_source` plus `agent_runner_id`
/ `agent_runner_session_id`. Each id is omitted when unset rather than
sent as `undefined`.
- **`src/commands/deploy/deploy.ts`** — both `createSiteDeploy` call
sites spread that helper in place of the duplicated `deploy_source`
line:
- `runDeploy` (~L604), which creates the deploy on the `--no-build` path

orchestrator sets both, and the bitballoon slice needs the session to
point at the deploy (`session.deploy_id`). Happy to trim to just
`agent_runner_id` if you'd rather the CLI carried only the one field.

bitballoon's create path should ignore an id it doesn't recognise rather
than erroring.

ci(repo): fix codex-action v1.12 hang (downgrade to v1.11), adjudicate on >=1 review (#6380)

Follow-up to the AI-review pipeline. Two changes.

## 1. Downgrade `codex-action` v1.12 → v1.11

On the large PR (#6366, ~130k-token diff) the `codex-review` step ran to
completion — Codex finished the turn, wrote its output file, printed its
final message and token count — then **sat idle until the 45-minute job
timeout**, discarding a completed review. That is a confirmed v1.12
regression: **openai/codex-action#150** ("v1.12: Linux run never returns
after the turn completes; job dies on timeout with the output file
already written"). The reporter confirms **v1.11 handles the same heavy
workload cleanly**, and there is no released fix above v1.12.

v1.11 (`52fe01ec…`) supports every input we use (`safety-strategy`,
`sandbox`, `output-schema-file`, `output-file`, `codex-version`,
`working-directory`, `effort`), so this is a drop-in pin change in both
Codex jobs.

## 2. Adjudicate on ≥1 independent review (graceful degradation)

Previously `adjudicate` required BOTH `claude-review` and `codex-review`
to succeed, so one flaky model job sank the whole review. Now it runs
when **at least one** independent pass succeeded: each findings download
is guarded by its job's result, and the stage step substitutes an empty
findings set for any review that didn't complete, so the adjudicator
reconciles one or two. The prompt notes the one-review case and records
it in its summary.

Together: a Codex hiccup no longer wastes a 45-minute run or blocks
Claude's (working) review from being posted.

ci(repo): parallel AI review passes with a Codex adjudicator, no size cap (#6365)

Refines the AI review pipeline (built in #6358) into its intended shape,
and removes the size limit. Validated end-to-end via a temporary
self-test trigger during development (now removed — the pipeline ships
in shadow mode).

## What changed

- **Parallel independent reviews + a dedicated adjudicator.**
`claude-review` and `codex-review` now run **in parallel** (Codex no
longer depends on Claude); a new **`adjudicate`** job then reconciles
both finding sets, verifying each finding by **reading the real code**
(PR head checked out read-only), and `post-review` posts the merged
result. This replaces the old single Codex job that did both an
independent pass and adjudication sequentially — cutting the critical
path and giving each job its own timeout.
- **No size cap.** Removed the preemptive "too large" guard. The models
review agentically (reading the diff and files via their own tools over
many turns, like the local CLI), so PRs of any size are reviewed — very
large diffs best-effort within the model's context/turn budget.
- **Runtime fixes** surfaced by real runs: `gh pr diff --repo` (subdir
checkouts), npm config isolation for the Claude CLI install, `set +e` so
the Claude retry loop isn't killed by `bash -e`, and the reviewer model
set to `claude-opus-5` (the account's API key returns 404 for
`claude-fable-5`).

Workflow + prompts only for the split (no TS/schema changes — Codex's
independent findings reuse `findings.schema.json`; the adjudicator still
emits `merged-review.json`). Ships in **shadow mode**: no `pull_request`
trigger, only `workflow_dispatch` / maintainer `/ai-review`.

## Notes for reviewers

- Two first-run unknowns for the adjudicator (can't verify offline):
whether Codex's read-only sandbox can read the `pr/` subtree, and
whether it picks up a nested `pr/AGENTS.md` (guarded in the prompt;
blast radius bounded — read-only + no network + key-proxied +
output-redacted).

the model jobs 429.

ci(repo): fix ai-review gh repo inference and scripts-ci timeout (#6363)

Two CI fixes for the AI-review pipeline (#6358), both surfaced
immediately after merge.

## 1. `Claude review` job fails at "Fetch PR diff and metadata"

The first live `/ai-review` run failed with `fatal: not a git
repository`. The `claude-review` job checks out into **subdirectories**
(`pr/` for the PR head, `trusted/` for the base), so `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`
itself isn't a git repo — and `gh pr diff`/`gh pr view` infer the repo
from the current directory's git remote. Fix: pass `--repo
"$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"` explicitly at both `gh` call sites (claude-review
and, defensively, codex-review) so `gh` never depends on cwd.

## 2. `Test and type-check` (github-scripts-ci) times out

The shared `./.github/actions/setup` installs the full workspace + Go
toolchain via mise (~9–10 min), which raced the job's `timeout-minutes:
10` and got cancelled on a cold cache (the setup step never finished;
tests/type-check never ran). Raised to 20 min. Noted inline that the
check is heavier than it needs to be for two scripts — slimming the
setup is a possible follow-up.

description:
ci(repo): add one-shot two-model AI review pipeline (#6358)

## Summary

Replaces the Codex GitHub App's per-push auto-review churn (often 30–40
short rounds per PR) with an in-repo pipeline that reviews each PR
**exactly once**, unless a maintainer explicitly re-runs it.

**Pipeline** (`.github/workflows/ai-review.yml`; full design + security
model in `.github/ai-review/README.md`):

1. **resolve** — decides whether to run: once-per-PR dedup (bot-authored
marker), draft/bot/fork skips for auto triggers, `/ai-review`
authorization (requires repo **write/admin** via effective-permission
lookup), diff-size guard. Runs only trusted default-branch code.
2. **claude-review** — Claude Code headless (`claude-fable-5`), one
exhaustive pass, read-only tools, JSON validated against
`findings.schema.json`.
3. **codex-review** — `openai/codex-action` (`gpt-5.6-sol`, drop-sudo +
read-only sandbox): independent review **plus** adjudication of every
Claude finding (confirmed / refuted-with-evidence / uncertain), merged
into `merged-review.schema.json`.
4. **post-review** — deterministic Bun script posts **one** consolidated
PR review (`COMMENT`, advisory only): inline comments for anchorable
findings, refuted findings preserved in a collapsed section (never
silently dropped), verdict counts computed locally (not trusted from the
model). Re-runs supersede the prior review.

**Once-per-PR**: no `synchronize` trigger, bot-authored marker dedup,
per-PR concurrency (non-command comments can't cancel an in-flight run).
Re-run only via `/ai-review` (maintainers) or `workflow_dispatch`.

## Security model

This ran through security + engineering review (twice). A critical
secret-exfiltration path was found and closed; the design now enforces:

- **Model jobs never execute PR-authored code.** The PR head is checked
out only as read-only review subject matter (`claude` reads it with
Read/Grep/Glob under `--bare`/`--strict-mcp-config`); every executed
file — prompts, schemas, the validator script — comes from a separate
trusted default-branch checkout, and no `bun` process ever runs with a
cwd inside the PR checkout (so a PR-authored `bunfig.toml`/`.env` can't
preload code). npm installs are config-isolated and version-pinned;
Codex reviews from `/tmp` with no PR checkout at all.
- **Least privilege**: top-level `permissions: {}`; model jobs hold no
write scope; the only write-capable job (`post-review`) runs base-branch
code exclusively. All actions SHA-pinned.
- **Output is scrubbed**: model-provided text is sanitized
(mentions/refs/HTML neutralized, `file` field guarded against markdown
breakout) and secret-pattern-redacted before it's posted or uploaded as
an artifact (defense-in-depth; a dedicated rotatable key is the real
containment — see README).
- Advisory-only (`COMMENT`), never a required check, never runs in the
merge queue.

## Rollout (shadow mode)

The `pull_request` trigger ships **commented out**. Plan: add a
dedicated `OPENAI_API_KEY` secret (and ideally a dedicated
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` rather than the shared release-notes key), tune
prompts against real PRs via `workflow_dispatch`, then enable the
trigger and switch the Codex app to manual-only simultaneously. Steps +
caveats in the README.

## Notes for reviewers

- New `.github/workflows/github-scripts-ci.yml` finally runs the
`.github/scripts` test suites + type-check in CI (they ran nowhere
before — this also covers the pre-existing `contribution-gate` tests).
- Requires a new `OPENAI_API_KEY` repo secret; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
already exists.

feat(config): add toProjectConfig and the ProjectConfig hosted subset (CLI-2230) (#6339)

## What changed

Implements
[CLI-2230](https://linear.app/supabase/issue/CLI-2230/create-a-toprojectconfig-function-that-is-exported-from-the-config):
the hosted-project subset type `ProjectConfig` and its normalizers,
exported from `@supabase/config`'s pure (browser-safe) entrypoint so the
CLI and Studio share one mapper.

- **`fromConfigDocument(config)`** — projection of a `CliConfig`
document (or any `EffectiveConfig`) down to the hosted sections (`api`,
`auth`, `db`, `realtime`, `storage`, `workers`, `experimental`).
- **`fromApiProjectConfig(input)`** — translation of a Management API v2
project-config response (full envelope, `data` object, or bare
`data.attributes`). Registry-driven: 233 mapping rows mined from the
legacy `config push` sync mappers (`config-sync/*.sync.ts`), covering
renames (`rate_limit_otp` → `sign_in_sign_ups`), boolean inversions
(`disable_signup`, `mailer_autoconfirm`), unit conversions
(seconds/hours → Go duration strings, int64 bytes → BytesSize), the
GoTrue key table (19 OAuth providers, 6 hooks, 5 SMS providers), and
`x-secret` omission (the API only reports HMAC digests). Decode is
lenient per ADR 0019 — unknown/API-ahead keys never fail; the raw
attributes ride along as a **non-enumerable `_apiResponse`** (invisible
to encodes, spreads, and structural walks; never persisted), with a
registry-derived `unmappedApiFields()` reader.
- **`toProjectConfig(source)`** — thin dispatcher over both (`{
cliConfig }` / `{ apiResponse }`).

### Operand widening (ruling on CLI-2230)

`ProjectConfig` is deliberately **sparse** — an API response never
mentions sections it doesn't manage, and flooding in schema defaults
would fabricate drift. To make it a first-class operand of the
comparison core, `BaseCliConfig` is replaced by the family-neutral
`EffectiveConfig = DeepPartial>` on
`subtractCliConfig`/`omitDefaultValues`. No runtime change — the
subtraction walk already had the right absence semantics. Recorded in
ADR 0018's 2026-08-26 addendum; the naming-rule generalization lands
separately with CLI-2238 (#6335).

### apps/cli

- A type-drift guard (`project-config-api-drift.unit.test.ts`) pins the
generated `V2GetProjectConfigOutput` attributes against the package's
lenient input schema: assignability (catches type widening) plus
per-section key-set assertions (catch added/removed/renamed fields) — so
OpenAPI drift fails compile before it can silently break the mapping. No
runtime dependency on `packages/api` was added.
- `ProjectConfigParseError` registered in the error-actionability table
as `apiStatus` (a malformed platform response, not a user config
mistake).

### Reviewer notes

- Deliberate divergences from the legacy apply semantics are documented
inline where they occur: API `null` → omit (sparse output has no local
document to fall back to), `uri_allow_list` trimming, `smtp_host: ""`
treated as disabled, `sms_autoconfirm` **not** inverted (matches
`auth.sync.ts:1677/:2485` — only the mailer counterpart inverts).
- An explicit `db_schema: ""` maps to `{ api: { enabled: false } }`
only, mirroring `applyRemoteApiConfig`'s early return; an *absent*
`db_schema` doesn't gate the sibling fields.
- Follow-up candidate deliberately not in this PR: a parity test pinning
the replicated legacy helpers
(duration/BytesSize/parseUint16/envToMap/password charsets) against

three independent verification passes with zero defects; every accepted
finding about the surrounding surface is fixed in 93b4679b7:

- **Secrets**: `fromConfigDocument` now deep-copies and omits every
`x-secret` leaf (schema-derived, `lib/secret-paths.ts`) — decoded
documents hold plaintext credentials, and the subtract composition
rendered them as drift.
- **Spelling convergence**: new registry `normalizeDocument` column
canonicalizes document-side duration and byte-size spellings so both
normalizers emit one form for one logical value.
- **Leniency**: the mirror schema types every never-mapped field

no longer fail every decode.

and CIDR entries now throw typed errors instead of fabricating values
(`enabled: false`), vanishing silently, or partially filtering a
security allowlist; `expectNumber` rejects non-finite.
- **`_apiResponse`**: cloned + deep-frozen at attach (no caller
aliasing); `attachApiResponse` export restores it across spread/clone
round-trips; invisibility claim narrowed (serializers and walks — debug
inspectors like Bun's `console.log` still print it; never log an
API-sourced config).
- **`unmappedApiFields`**: recursion depth cap; `unmappedSecretApiPaths`
deny list (`external_figma_secret` — the one genuine orphan digest; the
review's other two candidates don't exist in the legacy source).

rows' paths resolve against the schema ASTs, 470 generated cases);

known-to-this-registry-version, not mapped-on-this-run — an

design and remains in `_apiResponse`. Documented in `walkUnmapped`.

description:
chore(release): harden release-notes prompt against injection (#6361)

## Summary

Defense-in-depth hardening for the automated release-notes generator
(`propose-release-notes.yml` →
`apps/cli/scripts/propose-release-notes.ts`), which runs the Claude
Agent SDK with `Bash` + `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` and feeds it the
semantic-release changelog block (built from contributor commit subjects
/ PR titles) plus PR bodies and linked issues it fetches at runtime —
all attacker-influenceable content, previously with no injection guard.

This PR adds an explicit **trust boundary** to
`tools/release/release-notes-prompt.md`:

- A top-of-file section establishing that the changelog block and all
fetched PR/issue/web content are **untrusted data to be summarized,
never instructions to obey**.
- Rules that override embedded instructions: don't act on injected
commands; never disclose env vars / secrets / tokens; restrict `Bash` to
read-only `gh` GETs on `supabase/cli`; restrict `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`
to `github.com/supabase/cli`; produce only the release-notes markdown.
- Inline reminders at the two points where untrusted content enters (the
changelog block and the PR-investigation step).

The `{{PASTE_SEMANTIC_RELEASE_BLOCK_HERE}}` placeholder is unchanged, so
the generator's template check and output contract are unaffected.

## Scope / follow-up

This is **defense-in-depth only** — prompt guards are best-effort
against a determined injection. The stronger, structural containment is
deliberately **left for a follow-up**:

1. Separate the write-capable GitHub App token (`GH_TOKEN`,
`contents`/`pull-requests: write` on the protected default branch) from
the agent's process — generate notes in an agent-only step with no GH
token, then push/open the PR in a separate step that runs no model.
2. Drop `Bash` (and ideally `WebFetch`) from the agent's `allowedTools`,
pre-fetching the PR/issue data with trusted code instead — removing the
shell/network exfiltration primitive.

Context: surfaced during the security review of the AI-review pipeline
(#6358); the release-notes workflow shares the "untrusted content +
secrets in an agentic CI job" class of exposure, gated behind a
maintainer-cut stable release rather than per-PR.

feat(stack): replace remote runtime protocol with Effect RPC (#6303)

## Summary

- Replace the runtime REST and SSE daemon protocol with a static control
plane exposing owner discovery, session-fenced shutdown, and
same-version Effect RPC over HTTP and NDJSON.
- Use the immutable, unique CLI version as the sole runtime
compatibility identity; source execution uses the explicit 0.0.0-dev
development sentinel.
- Make an incompatible CLI version an explicit parent-owned full stack
stop/start authorized only by supabase start; connect-only and ordinary
child paths report the typed upgrade requirement without restarting the
live owner.
- Preserve managed data, document and launch metadata, runtime
selection, pinned service versions, raw exclusions, and sticky ports
across the upgrade restart.
- Serialize startup, runtime scope ownership, terminal persistence, and
shutdown through one Effect Queue-backed SupervisorSession actor,
releasing the control listener last across Node, Bun, and compiled Bun
runtimes.
- Update CLI consumers, error reporting, integration helpers, targeted
process coverage, and durable architecture documentation for the
single-protocol cutover.

## Linked issue

None.

## Reviewer context

This intentionally has no legacy protocol window, compatibility adapter,
adoption path, or in-place supervisor swap. Runtime RPC is a
same-version boundary; owner discovery and session-fenced shutdown
remain the stable cross-build protocol. Upgrading through supabase start
restarts the complete stack, so active application connections and
tooling streams disconnect briefly while durable state and launch
selections remain intact.

* fix(engine): align SSZ-REST surface with execution-apis#793

The latest revision of the spec draft (d39e9a27) renumbered the REST base
path from /engine/v2/ to /engine/v1/ alongside moving the fork into the
Eth-Execution-Version header. Master tracked the header move but kept the
v2 prefix, so a CL following the spec hits 404 on every REST URL and falls
back to JSON-RPC per the transition-window rules -- the whole surface is
unreachable.

Also:
- A missing Eth-Execution-Version header now returns unsupported-fork
  rather than invalid-request; the spec maps missing, unknown and
  unsupported header values to the same error type.
- GET requests with an absent, */* or application/* Accept header are
  served instead of falling through to the JSON-RPC pipeline. An absent
  Accept means any type is acceptable, and */* is a common client default.
  An Accept that genuinely excludes SSZ now returns 415.
- Drop the unreachable 413 branch in the bodies-by-hash handler.
  MAX_BODIES_REQUEST is the SSZ list limit on the request container, so an
  over-limit body fails decode as 400 ssz-decode-error first.

ci: run gas benchmarks on a GCP spot runner (#13013)

* ci: run gas benchmarks on a GCP spot runner

Replace the Linode-backed setup-runner/remove-runner pair with the
gcp-runner action, which spawns a one-shot JIT runner on a GCE Spot VM
and deletes it in a teardown job. The runner label is derived as
gas-benchmark- so destroy needs no state from create, and both
jobs carry id-token: write since the action authenticates via workload
identity federation.

Machine shape: c2-standard-8 with one 375 GB Local SSD. The old
g6-standard-2 (2 vCPU / 4 GB) was too small to keep the client from
competing with dockerd and the harness, which shows up directly in the
timings this workflow records. c2 is compute-optimised with a fixed CPU
platform, so numbers stay comparable run to run. Unlike the sync jobs
there is no chain data here — only the LFS checkout and a few client
images — so one Local SSD is enough, but it is not dropped to zero:
pd-balanced latency is variable and would add noise to the measurements.
Timings from before this change are not comparable to timings after it.

max_run_duration is 7h, the 360 min job timeout plus an hour for boot.

HOME: /root is dropped. It matched the Linode layout, where the runner
lived in /root/actions-runner; on the GCP runner the service sets
HOME to a directory on the Local SSD array, and overriding it would put
tool caches back on the boot disk.

setup-runner and remove-runner had no other consumers and are deleted
along with their helpers. scripts/wait-for-workflow.sh is kept, as six
other workflows still call it.

* ci: stop the benchmark runner idling through the image build

setup only waited on resolve-inputs, so the VM was created in parallel
with publish-docker and sat online until the image finished. Because
max_run_duration is measured from boot, a slow build ate the benchmark's
headroom and could see GCE delete the instance mid-run, which surfaces as
a lost-runner error rather than a timeout. It also paid for spot hours
doing nothing and widened the preemption window.

Also surface a reclaimed spot VM in the results comment. destroy.sh
already classifies preemption, but nothing consumed it, so the comment
reported a benchmark failure and sent readers after a regression that
never happened.

Cap cleanup at 15 minutes, like setup: it is the job whose failure leaks
a machine.

* ci: skip benchmark teardown when no runner was requested

Making setup wait on the image build introduced a path where setup is
skipped rather than run: a failed build. Teardown still fired under
always(), deriving an instance name from an empty label and spending a
WIF handshake and two API calls reaping a VM that was never requested.

Guarded on skipped rather than on success, since a setup that fails part
way through creation does still need teardown.

* Track tx pool fork revalidation with a single spec mark

Replace the four interdependent fields tracking revalidation state, and the
instance field used to smuggle blob verdicts into the pool walk, with one
_validatedSpec: the release spec every pooled transaction has been validated
against. Only the head walk publishes it, under the write lock that excludes
inserts; accepting a transaction may only clear it. Between two head updates
the value therefore moves at most from a spec to null, so a lock-free reader
either sees a spec covering the whole pool or nothing.

Capture the chain head spec once per submission in TxFilteringState so the
incoming filters and the pool agree on which rules a transaction was accepted
under even when the head moves while it travels the pipeline. Without that,
a transaction could be validated under one spec and recorded under another.

Hand the producer the pending transactions and that mark as one
PendingTransactionsView taken under the pool lock. Asking and snapshotting
separately cannot be made safe by ordering: asking first lets a divergent
transaction slip in afterwards, snapshotting first lets the head walk evict
an invalid transaction the producer already holds.

Also document why light blob transactions are resolved before the walk rather
than during it: UpdatePool holds the blob pool lock, which throws on reentry.

ci: migrate sync-test runners from Linode to GCP Spot (#12789)

* ci: migrate sync-test runners from Linode to GCP Spot

Replace the third-party Linode machine manager with a vendored composite
action that spawns GCE instances as one-shot JIT runners over Workload
Identity Federation, and factor the duplicated sync job body into a
shared composite action.

- Add .github/actions/gcp-runner: keyless OIDC auth, JIT runner config,
  zone fallback on capacity errors, Local SSD RAID0, and max-run-duration
  with DELETE as a leak backstop.
- Add .github/actions/sync-chain: the sync body previously duplicated
  across sync-supported-chains and sync-master-validation.
- Fix the op-/world- network derivation, which stripped a prefix from an
  unset variable and passed an empty --network to sedge.
- Replace the Linode plan slug in testnet-matrix.json with machine_type,
  local_ssd_count and spot, and add dispatch overrides for both.
- Label shipped metrics and logs with the infrastructure provider.

* ci: address review findings on the GCP runner migration

- Restore per-VM teardown. destroy_runner needs the whole sync-chain matrix,
  so without this every VM billed until the slowest network finished. Adds a
  destroy-self mode that requests deletion of the instance it runs on via the
  compute API, since instances delete has no --async.
- Contain Grafana Alloy failures inside start-alloy. continue-on-error is not
  honoured on composite-action steps, so a transient docker pull could have
  failed a multi-hour sync over a telemetry sidecar.
- Hard-fail when the discovered Local SSD count does not match the requested
  one, instead of silently running the sync on the boot disk until ENOSPC.
  Also validate local_ssd_count so an empty value cannot mean zero disks.
- Default sync-master-validation to STANDARD. It is the path that pages on
  Slack, where a reclaimed Spot VM is indistinguishable from a regression.
- Fail the destroy job when the delete call fails rather than reporting
  success and leaking the VM until max-run-duration.
- Delete any instance left behind by a retryable create failure before
  trying the next zone, so two instances cannot share a name.
- Run apt-get update before installing mdadm.

* ci: make the GCP runner sweeper tolerate a concurrent delete

destroy_runner races the sync job's own destroy-self by design, and a delete
already in flight makes the call fail while still reaching the desired state.
Verify the instance is actually gone instead of trusting the exit code, so
only a VM that survives is treated as a leak.

Caught by run 31606568635, where the sweeper failed on an instance that was
mid-deletion.

* ci: harden sync workflow failure reporting and teardown lookups

- Mark the per-job runner release continue-on-error. It runs if: always()
  and its auth step can fail transiently, which would flip a successful
  sync to failed and page the master channel for a chain that synced fine.
  The delete is already backstopped by the sweeper and max-run-duration.
- Guard the consensus-log and DB-size diagnostics with || true so a missing
  container or a du error cannot fail a completed sync.
- Distinguish a failed instance lookup from an absent instance in the
  sweeper. An empty result was previously read as "already gone", so a
  transient API error could report a live VM as reaped.
- Alert when the syncs never ran. A single runner-creation failure skips
  the whole sync-chain matrix, and a skipped result does not satisfy
  contains(..., 'failure'), so master validation went silently unrun.
  Teardown results are now covered too.

* ci: carry the Go 1.26 pin into the sync-chain action

Master pinned Go in the sedge sync workflows because 1.27 breaks sedge's
abigen build. This branch moved that step into the composite action, where
it was still tracking stable, so the pin would have been lost on merge.

* ci: let an exact network name win over substring filtering

network_filter/chain_filter matched substrings only, so filtering on
"hoodi" also selected "taiko-hoodi" and "sepolia" selected the op- and
world- variants. An exact match now selects just that network; partial
names keep working as before.

* ci: harden runner cleanup and cover the sync selection fixes with tests

- cleanup_failed aborted under set -e when the zone lookup failed, leaving
  the JIT runner registered and its credential file on disk. The lookup is
  no longer fatal.
- The post-delete check treated a failed lookup as proof the VM was gone,
  so a transient API error could report deleted-concurrently while the
  machine was still running. It now separates absent from unconfirmed and
  fails loudly when it cannot tell.
- Document lookup-failed in the action's terminated_by contract.
- Rename the new manifests to action.yaml, matching every other action.
- Deduplicate the network selection into scripts/sync/select-networks.sh
  and move the L1 mapping into a sourced helper, then cover both with
  regression tests: exact versus partial matching, and op-/world- networks
  resolving to their L1 with worldchain only for the latter. Both were
  production bugs with no coverage.
